additional_open_research_occurrences.topic: Exponential subsolutions at zero individual threshold
additional_open_research_occurrences.exact_source_line: The next estimate quantifies this scalar error when the density root is approximable by bounded roots. Whether an exponential subsolution exists when $b_h(f)=0$ is a separate question; \cref{thm:individual-exponential-subsolution} applies whenever such a subsolution is available.

additional_open_research_occurrences.topic: Exact individual normalized equation at the attained threshold
additional_open_research_occurrences.exact_source_line: The distinction is caused by the order restriction on a smooth test: it cannot use a measurable increase of a density whose essential lower value is unchanged in every open set. Bounded measurable tests retain this information. The theorem concerns subsolution existence for individual $L^1$ densities. A characterization of exact normalized equations at $b_h(f)$, including their natural singularity class and finite-mass compactness, remains a separate problem.
additional_open_research_occurrences.inventory_relationship: Expository occurrence of the existing formal problem, not a new formal question

additional_open_research_occurrences.topic: Equality of the bounded-root closure and admissible root space when lower mass vanishes
additional_open_research_occurrences.exact_source_line: The same tail estimate gives a uniform exponential-damping modulus and scalar error bounds in \cref{prop:exponential-root-tail-modulus}. It does not, by itself, give capacity convergence of equation potentials. When lower mass vanishes, equality of $\mathcal D_h^0$ and $\mathcal D_h$ remains a separate question.
